findings_qualitative.value: Multiple coherent wide-angle shells exist in both lobes, consistent with entrainment by an episodic wide-angle wind; shells are not formed by direct launching.

evidence.quote: Our results provide strong evidence that wide-angle disk winds can be episodic, just as protostellar jets.

claims.hypothesis: Wide-angle wind in HH 46/47 is episodic
claims.experiment: Identify and fit parabolic shells in 12CO (2-1) PPV and PV data
claims.result: At least two shells per lobe with age spacing of 210-320 yr
claims.finding: Shells arise from repeated wide-angle wind outbursts matching the jet knot interval

evidence.quote: The intervals between consecutive outburst are found to be $(2-3)\times 10^2~\mathrm{yr}$

claims.hypothesis: Shells are entrained ambient gas rather than launched material
claims.experiment: Compare shell mass and momentum rates to jet/wind values
claims.result: Mass rates 1-2 orders higher, momentum rates similar

evidence.loc: Origin of the Multiple Shell Structure
evidence.quote: have mass loading rates that are one to two orders of magnitudes higher than the mass loss rates of the jet (or wind) launched from the disk

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Jet bow-shock entrainment judged unlikely for the shells, though not ruled out.

evidence.loc: Origin of the Multiple Shell Structure
evidence.quote: we think these shells are unlikely to be formed by jet entrainment

limitations_admitted.value: Dynamical ages may be upper limits; mass and momentum are lower limits

evidence.loc: Origin of the Multiple Shell Structure
evidence.quote: it is likely that the estimated dynamical ages are upper limits of their true ages.

referee_caveats_inferred: Best-fit selection by eye with no uncertainties on parameters
Single pointing truncates the outflow at ~20 arcsec

reproducibility.score_reason: Data are from a single project and the basic imaging is described, but the shell fitting is visual and many parameters are missing.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: Main results depend on visual shell identification and by-eye fitting, and the public status of the data is not stated in the paper.
